note: Definitions shown behind the i button on every field. Sources: David Kirsh's ratified criteria (gold-20 adjudication, AF-first spec, HITL onboarding). Multiple labels may genuinely apply to one paper: record the best single label in the verdict/correction, and put any additional true labels in 'Also applies'.

article_type.definition: What kind of paper this is, judged by how its knowledge was produced — not by its topic.

values.empirical_quantitative: Collects data and reports numbers or statistical tests.
values.empirical_qualitative: Collects data through interviews, observation, or thematic analysis; no statistical testing at its core.
values.mixed_methods: Substantial quantitative AND qualitative components in one study.
values.narrative_review: Synthesizes other papers' findings without a systematic search. David's criterion: a paper offering pointers and associations but no theory is a review.
values.systematic_review: A review that describes its database search and inclusion criteria.
values.meta_analysis: Statistically combines results from prior studies.
values.theoretical: Builds or defends a theory. Required: an actual theory, not pointers and associations.
values.methodology: The paper's primary contribution is a method, instrument, protocol, or analysis approach that others could use.
values.empirical_research: Machine's label — an empirical study; decide yourself whether quantitative, qualitative, or mixed, and correct to the specific one.
values.methods: Machine's label — read as methodology: the paper's primary contribution is a method, instrument, or protocol.
values.commentary: A response or commentary on another publication.

article_type.multi: A paper can honestly be two of these (e.g. methodology + empirical_quantitative: it develops a method AND runs an ordinary experiment). Judge the machine's single label on its merits; add other true labels under 'Also applies'.

apa_citation.definition: The full APA-style reference for THIS paper itself: authors, year, title, journal or venue, volume/pages, DOI where printed. Judge against the paper's own front matter — the title page and its printed citation block — never from memory.

main_conclusion.definition: The paper's central finding or claim, as its authors would state it — one sentence. Not a side result, not a limitation, not the aim.

independent_variables.definition: What the MAIN study manipulated or used as predictors (e.g. lighting level, ceiling height, sound condition). Empty is correct for reviews and theory papers.

dependent_variables.definition: The outcomes the MAIN study measured (e.g. comfort rating, task accuracy, heart rate).

construct_pair.definition: The central exposure-to-outcome pairing at the construct level, as X → Y (e.g. 'daylight exposure → mood'). One pair — the paper's main axis, not every relation it touches.

direction.definition: The sign of the main IV→DV relation as the paper reports it.

values.positive: More of the IV goes with more of the DV.
values.negative: More of the IV goes with less of the DV.
values.mixed: The paper's own results point both ways across conditions or outcomes.
values.no_effect: The paper reports no reliable effect.
values.differential: Machine's label — the effect differs by subgroup or condition; usually better expressed as mixed, with the split named.
values.unclear: Machine's label — it could not determine a direction. Judge whether the paper itself is genuinely unclear or the machine simply missed it.
values.not_applicable: The paper makes no directional claim (reviews, theory, methods papers).

sample_n.definition: Total human participants in the MAIN study. If several studies are reported, the primary one. Null is correct when no human sample exists.

p_value.definition: The p value attached to the MAIN finding, exactly as printed (e.g. 'p < .001'). Null is correct if the paper reports none.

effect_size.definition: The main finding's effect size as printed (d, r, η², odds ratio...). Null is correct if none is reported. A number that could not be an effect size (d = 57462037) is wrong on its face.

stimulus_description.definition: What participants were actually exposed to — rooms, images, sounds, VR scenes, light settings — in a sentence or two.

methods_surface_summary.definition: Design, procedure, and analysis in brief: what kind of experiment or study this was and how it was run.

measurement_inventory.definition: The named instruments and measures used (e.g. PANAS, EEG alpha power, a 7-point comfort rating). Judge whether the list matches what the methods section actually names — missing instruments count against it.
